title: Flat Noetherian model retaining a specified polynomial presentation
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $n\ge0$, and fix a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exist a subring $R_0\subseteq R$ generated by finitely many elements as a $\mathbf Z$-algebra, a flat finitely presented $R_0$-algebra $A_0$, a surjection $\pi_0:P_0=R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A_0$, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:A_0\otimes_{R_0}R\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ such that, under $P_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong P$, the map $\alpha\circ(\pi_0\otimes1)$ is the prescribed $\pi$. The rings $R_0,P_0,A_0$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. No flatness of $R_0\to R$ or injectivity of $A_0\to A$ is asserted. Zero rings and $n=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02JO, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, especially eventual flatness (3), with finite relation-coefficient descent preserving the prescribed polynomial map; Noetherian permanence Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence. Agent formulation retaining the presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] to the given surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A$. Its hypotheses are exactly finite presentation of $A/R$, finite $n$, and the prescribed surjectivity. Choose $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ generating $\ker\pi$, allowing $m=0$. Thus evaluation through $\pi$ identifies $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ with $A$: the induced map is onto because $\pi$ is, and a class maps to zero exactly when its representative is in $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$.

source.place: Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent; the elementary quotient identification following the prescribed surjection.

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq R$ be the $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by all coefficients of the finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_m$. Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $T\subseteq R$ containing $C$, ordered by inclusion, and designate $C$ as its initial index. This is a small nonempty directed set: $C$ is an index, and the subring generated by the union of two finite generating sets is an upper bound. The finite-type subalgebra colimit of [lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras] remains $R$ on this subsystem: any finite-type subalgebra $U$ lies in the subring generated by $U$ and $C$, which is an index. Equivalently, any $r\in R$ belongs to the index generated by $C$ and $r$; compatible maps from these subrings glue to a unique ring map from $R$, with addition and multiplication checked in a common index.

source.place: Tag 02JO (3), choice of a directed coefficient-subring system; explicit cofinal restriction of the system in lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras.

proof.text: For every $T\in I$ put $P_T=T[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $B_T=P_T/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, viewing the coefficients in $T$, with quotient map $q_T$. These are actual quotient rings [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and the displayed finite presentation makes $B_T/T$ finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Coefficient inclusions give maps $B_T\to B_U$. For $T\subseteq U$ the canonical comparison $U\otimes_T B_T\to B_U$ sends $u\otimes[p]\mapsto u[p]$. It is an isomorphism: first identify $U\otimes_T P_T$ with $P_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], then pass to the quotient by the images of the $f_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Here $(U\otimes_TP_T)\otimes_{P_T}B_T=U\otimes_TB_T$ via $(u\otimes p)\otimes b\mapsto u\otimes pb$, inverse $u\otimes b\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes b$. Both comparisons therefore send coefficients and each variable class to themselves. The identical calculation with $U=R$, followed by step 1, gives an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\beta_T:R\otimes_TB_T\to A$, $r\otimes[p]\mapsto r\pi(p)$.

source.place: Tag 02JO (3)(a)-(b), same-relations base change; polynomial base change and Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, for the quotient comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] to the directed base-ring system $T\in I$ of step 2, with initial index $C$, initial algebras $B_0=C$ and $C_0=B_C$, and initial map the structure map $C\to B_C$. This map is finitely presented by step 3. Its stage map is $T\to T\otimes_CB_C\cong B_T$, by the comparisons of step 3. Its limit map is $R\to R\otimes_CB_C\cong A$ and is flat by hypothesis: the comparison is $R$-linear and tensoring it gives commuting isomorphisms in the injectivity test defining flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The cited node thus supplies an index $T_0\supseteq C$ for which $T_0\to B_{T_0}$ is flat. No flatness of the transition inclusions is a hypothesis of that node.

source.place: Tag 02JO, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat (3), specialized to the algebra as its own module via lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map.

proof.text: Take $R_0=T_0$, $P_0=P_{T_0}$, $A_0=B_{T_0}$ and $\pi_0=q_{T_0}$. Surjectivity of $\pi_0$ is the quotient-map clause of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; finite presentation and flatness were proved in steps 3 and 4. Define $\alpha:A_0\otimes_{R_0}R\to A$ by $b\otimes r\mapsto r\beta_{T_0}(1\otimes b)$, the isomorphism $\beta_{T_0}$ preceded by tensor-factor exchange. The exchange and its inverse both send $b\otimes r$ to $r\otimes b$ and are well-defined by the balancing relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under $P_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong P$, $p\otimes r$ corresponds to $rp$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], and $\alpha((\pi_0\otimes1)(p\otimes r))=r\pi(p)=\pi(rp)$. Pure tensors generate, so the composite is the prescribed $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 02JO (3), final model; direct check of the prescribed presentation on pure tensors (agent refinement).

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal has a least positive element $d$; Euclidean division shows every element is a multiple of $d$, while the zero ideal is generated by $0$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] first to $\mathbf Z\to R_0$, which has the finite generating set in the definition of $I$, then to the polynomial ring $R_0\to P_0$, and finally to the quotient $R_0\to A_0$, generated by the images of its $n$ variables. This proves all three Noetherian assertions. The construction allows empty variable and relation lists; if $A=0$, the kernel generators can include $1$, so the same quotient construction applies; if $R=0$, its only unital subring is itself. There is no use of an injective map $A_0\to A$ or of flatness of $R_0\to R$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, finite-type clause, and the elementary ideal argument for the integers; edge cases of Tag 02JO (3).

proof_origin.place: Tags 00R2 and 02JO (3), retaining the prescribed polynomial generators and relation coefficients; Tag 00FN for Noetherianity. The pure-tensor compatibility and coefficient-subring restriction are written out here.
